source_text:
παθεῖν· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὁ χορὸς τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐπανῄεσαν ἐκ τοῦ συνεδρίου τῶν
Ἰουδαίων, χαίροντες, οὐ διὰ τὴν βασιλείαν μόνον τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ' ὅτι
κατηξιώθησαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ ἀτιμασθῆναι· καὶ αὐτὸ γὰρ τοῦτο καὶ καθ'
ἑαυτὸ, μεγίστη τιμὴ καὶ στέφανος καὶ βραβεῖον καὶ ἡδονῆς ὑπόθεσις ἀμαράντου· οὐ
thought_title: The apostles' joy in dishonor for Jesus' name
orientation: Olympiodorus is explaining why suffering for the truth is itself a prize, and now turns to the example of the apostles rejoicing after being dishonored by the Jewish council.
pass_a_gloss: to suffer; because of this also the chorus of the apostles went up from the council of the Jews, rejoicing, not because of the kingdom only of the heavens, but because they were counted worthy on behalf of the name of Jesus to be dishonored; and this very thing indeed also by itself, [is] greatest honor and crown and prize and of pleasure a source unfading; not

choices.why: Keeps the collective image of a chorus, which conveys the unified group rejoicing together.
The verb means to go up or return; 'went up' preserves the directional sense from the council.
The passive of καταξιόω means to be deemed or counted worthy; this rendering keeps the sense of divine or official estimation.
The glossary requires 'dishonored' for this term, and the passive infinitive preserves the grammatical voice.
Keeps the noun 'source' for ὑπόθεσις and the adjective 'unfading' for ἀμαράντου, preserving the word order and the sense of an enduring origin of pleasure.

bible_refs.note: The apostles rejoiced after being dishonored for the name of Jesus, echoing Acts 5:41.

pass_b_english: For this reason the chorus of the apostles went up from the council of the Jews rejoicing—not only because of the kingdom of heaven, but because they had been counted worthy to be dishonored for the name of Jesus. This very thing, even by itself, is the greatest honor, and a crown, and a prize, and a source of unfading pleasure.

last_rejected.quote: For this reason the chorus of the apostles went up from the council of the Jews rejoicing
last_rejected.source_quote: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὁ χορὸς τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐπανῄεσαν ἐκ τοῦ συνεδρίου τῶν Ἰουδαίων, χαίροντες
last_rejected.why: English hides that Paul is speaking; source has λέγων earlier making this Paul's words.
last_rejected.fix: Paul continues: 'For this reason the chorus of the apostles went up...'
last_rejected.ruling: No λέγων in cited source; speaker attribution is editorial, not translation error in this passage.

last_rejected.quote: not only because of the kingdom of heaven
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐ διὰ τὴν βασιλείαν μόνον τῶν οὐρανῶν
last_rejected.why: Missing 'only' (μόνον); English loses exclusivity, weakening the 'not only...but' construction.
last_rejected.fix: not only because of the kingdom of heaven alone
last_rejected.ruling: English 'not only' already renders μόνον via the correlative 'not only...but' construction.
